newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: STATE COMMERCIAL BANK TENDER TERMS APPROVED.
newsitem.headline: STATE COMMERCIAL BANK TENDER TERMS APPROVED.

text.p: Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta said on Friday parliament's finance and budget committee okayed the terms of the tender for the sale of State Commercial Bank.
Lithuania's State commercial Bank is one of the two banks slated for privatisation by the country's government along with the Agricultural Bank.
"The budget and finance committee approved today the terms of the tender," Shemeta told Reuters.
"We also expect to receive a final approval from Bank of Lithuania today," Shemeta added.
The government said earlier this week it intends to announce the tender for the sale of State Commercial Bank next week.
"We expect to announce the participants of the bid which will be chosen as the potential winners of the tender before the end of June," Shemeta said.
"After the government takes a decision on the winner, the actual contract will be signed in 30 days," Shemeta said.
Shemeta said the participants of the bid would have to meet capital requirements set by the European Union.
"The buyer also shall have to take an obligation to invest in the bank so that the bank meets all the risk limiting requirements imposed by the Bank of Lithuania," Shemeta said.
The buyer will also have the right to carry out a merger, Shemeta added.
"If the buyer is a foreign bank it shall have the right to found its affiliate or branch in Lithuania on the basis of the State Commercial Bank," he added.
The government said earlier it planned to decide on the financial advisor for privatisation of the Agricultural Bank in August and to announce the tender at the beginning of 1998.
